conceptZh: 發條鯊魚為了輕按變形鈕卻過度上緊發條，一頭撞散機台上的七根構件排成「形」，最後輕碰按鈕讓自己變成圓滾滾的球。
object: A chunky wind-up toy shark and a small shape-changing press built from seven cobalt-blue stroke components.
morph: One overshooting collision tips seven rigid components into the exact strokes of 形; a gentle second button tap then rounds the shark into a ball.
creativeAngle: 把「形」的外觀概念化成看得見的變形機關；撞擊負責排出正確七畫，輕按才讓鯊魚變圓，形成大力失敗、小力成功的反差。
promptEn:
Create an 8-second stylized 3D cartoon in one locked, nearly frontal view on a pale apricot floor and background. Cast an original chunky wind-up toy shark: turquoise plastic, oversized harmless teeth, tiny rubber feet, an exposed brass winding key, and a wildly overconfident grin. Its sole prop is a compact shape-changing press with a tiny coral button on a low side extension and seven solid cobalt-blue structural pieces. Bright soft lighting, crisp silhouettes, warm toy-scale slapstick.

0.0–1.6 seconds: The shark wants to press the tiny button. It squints at this minuscule job, proudly opens its enormous jaws, then bites its own winding key by mistake. Twisting around on dry land, it winds itself with ridiculous effort; the press's seven blue pieces begin rattling. The first spoken “形” lands as this rattling build begins.

1.6–3.1 seconds: Release! Its little feet whir and it rockets left to right, sailing straight over the button. Give it a split-second startled eye flick toward the missed target before one big, soft BONK against the press. Its snout squashes flat, its eyes wobble, and it rebounds with a dazed grin. The impact kicks all seven blue pieces outward and forward onto the central display plane.

3.1–4.7 seconds: The shark skids backward on smoking rubber feet, with two small wisps that immediately disappear. The pieces tumble only a short distance and settle through visible physical contact into the exact Traditional Chinese glyph 形. Use seven properly shaped strokes: the left 开 component has two horizontals, a left downward-falling stroke and a right vertical; three separate parallel falling strokes form 彡 on the right. Preserve the standard proportions, intersections and open spaces. The second spoken “形” coincides with the last piece seating at 4.4 seconds. By 4.7 seconds the completed glyph is perfectly still, centered, uncropped and approximately 70% of frame height.

4.7–8.0 seconds: Below the glyph, the chastened shark gives the surviving button one feather-light nose tap. Exactly as “變形” is spoken, its toy body smoothly rounds into a comically plump ball with the same fins, grin and winding key. It spins once on dry land, then beams proudly. Keep this small action entirely below the strokes; hold the finished glyph unchanged through the end.

Audio: warm, friendly off-screen Taiwanese Mandarin, slowly and distinctly, reading exactly “形、形、變形” (ㄒㄧㄥˊ、ㄒㄧㄥˊ、ㄅㄧㄢˋ ㄒㄧㄥˊ), at approximately 0.7, 4.4 and 6.0 seconds respectively. Clear tones and short pauses; stop after the word. Gentle winding, skid and padded bonk sounds beneath the voice. Only 形 appears as text; no captions, other lettering, logos, watermarks, flashing effects or extra dialogue.
